about: Golden set expected outcomes (ROADMAP L0). One entry per demo-mail.ps1 scenario, keyed tenant-name like the golden-snapshot.ps1 rows. 'expect' holds the snapshot fields a correct pipeline must produce: a value, or an array of acceptable values where the email is genuinely ambiguous; null and empty string both mean 'empty'; a field that is absent is not scored. urgency is written as LOW/NORMAL/HIGH (the snapshot's ordinal is mapped). 'draft' is the checklist for the reply text (must / must_not), judged by a human or an LLM judge in L1 - the snapshot holds no draft text. Facts behind the checklists come from the dev seeds: port-service tracking (V2/V3 sea, V7 road), carrier_rate and tenant_document (V31). Sell price = rate x (1 + margin%). Urgency and sentiment follow the classifier prompt (EmailClassificationService.typedRoutingPrompt): HIGH = time-critical, deadline, demurrage, stuck or held shipment, urgent/asap; NEGATIVE = angry, frustrated, complaining, threatening to leave.
